basis: P5CS-related metabolic spastic paraplegia. Cataracts vary by pedigree; early cataracts reported in 2/15 dominant cases in one series do not establish >=30% across the umbrella.

decisions.ocular: none: early cataracts reported in 2/15 dominant cases; not obligatory across SPG9. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4553756/).

basis: Sex cord-stromal granulosa lineage represents the gonadal endocrine compartment. Gynecomastia (~25%) and metastases (~20%) do not add organs.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: granulosa sex cord-stromal lineage is gonadal endocrine tissue; hormone symptoms are not required to label a tumour of this compartment.

basis: Cardiocutaneous degeneration defines LCPS; emphysema and intracranial hemorrhage each annotated 80-99%. Dyslipidemia omitted at cap; cancer predisposition does not add organs.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intracranial hemorrhage is annotated 80-99%, supporting common direct brain injury from the syndrome's vasculopathy rather than merely an increased future risk.

basis: Typhus infections target vascular endothelium and cause small-vessel vasculitis. Rash is transient; severe organ complications are not common across the umbrella.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection with small-vessel vasculitis is a central disease lesion. [CDC study](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/24/11/17-1373_article).

basis: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like brain injury. Sensorineural hearing loss occurs in ~58% of MELAS; extrapolated to MTTQ with subtype frequency uncertain.

decisions.otologic: involved: hearing loss ~58% in MELAS; extrapolated to MTTQ, with subtype-specific uncertainty. [Review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822652/).

basis: Chronic infection directly affects skin and peripheral nerves. Muscle atrophy (30-79%) is secondary to denervation; ocular and upper airway damage are below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy is annotated 30-79%, but usually results from peripheral nerve denervation rather than direct muscle infection or a defining myopathy.

basis: Congenital cranial dysinnervation defines ocular motor dysfunction; extraocular muscle atrophy/fibrosis is secondary. Systemic skeletal abnormalities are minority features.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: extraocular muscle changes follow cranial dysinnervation; a primary skeletal myopathy is not established. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1348/).

basis: Vitreoretinal B-cell lymphoma; direct CNS dissemination by the same lymphoma occurs in roughly 50-80% over the disease course, rather than representing an unrelated later malignancy.

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS dissemination of the same lymphoma occurs in most patients over its course. [AAO](https://eyewiki.aao.org/Primary_Vitreoretinal_Lymphoma).

basis: Luteinized ovarian stromal proliferation occupies the steroidogenic gonadal compartment. Its endocrine tissue origin supports the axis even when clinically asymptomatic and self-limited.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: inferred from the steroidogenic luteinized stromal lesion; virilization is not required. [Tissue study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9398748/).

basis: Glycosylation defect with encephalopathy and defining coagulopathy; cataract 30-79%/coloboma. Joint hypermobility (2/3) omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone lacks proven liver damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: coagulation abnormalities are explicitly defining and annotated 30-79%; the blood/coagulation mechanism rule requires primary assignment.
decisions.ocular: involved: defining coloboma/cataract (30-79%); metabolic and coagulation mechanisms plus severe neurodevelopmental disease take the three primary slots.
